limitations_and_boundaries: biolord assumes partial supervision over a limited set of known attributes; full disentanglement of all biological factors is not guaranteed.
The method relies on the availability of labeled attributes for training; performance may degrade with very few labeled attributes.
Counterfactual predictions are limited to the attribute combinations seen during training; extrapolation to entirely new attribute ranges may be unreliable.
The evaluation is limited to the specific datasets and perturbation types studied; generalizability to other single-cell modalities or perturbation types requires further validation.
The biolord-classify extension depends on the quality of partial labels and may propagate errors if initial labels are noisy.

experiments_or_tasks: Apply biolord to a spatiotemporal Plasmodium infection atlas to disentangle infection status from spatial and temporal attributes, and use counterfactual predictions to identify infection-associated gene programs.

Develop biolord, a deep generative model that learns disentangled representations of single-cell data by encoding known attributes (e.g., cell type, time, perturbation) and unknown attributes into a decomposed latent space, and training a generator to reconstruct observed measurements.
Evaluate biolord on drug response prediction using the sci-Plex 3 dataset, comparing counterfactual predictions for unseen drugs against baselines (naive, chemCPA, chemCPA-pre, PerturbNet).
Evaluate biolord on genetic perturbation prediction using two Perturb-seq datasets (one-gene and two-gene perturbations), comparing against GEARS.
Extend biolord to biolord-classify for semi-supervised attribute classification, and apply it to classify abortive hepatocytes at earlier time points in the Plasmodium infection atlas.

methods.name: biolord
methods.protocol_description: Deep generative framework that encodes single-cell measurements and known attribute labels into separate embeddings for each known attribute and one embedding for unknown attributes. A generator maps these embeddings back to the observed data. Training maximizes reconstruction accuracy while minimizing information in the unknown embedding via capacity constraints. For drug response, RDKit chemical features and dosage are used as ordered attributes; cell line is categorical. For genetic perturbations, GO term graph edge features are used as ordered attributes. Counterfactual predictions are generated by taking reference cells and modifying attribute labels to unseen values. biolord-classify extends the model with a classifier for each attribute to predict missing labels.

methods.name: chemCPA
methods.protocol_description: Baseline model for drug response prediction that trains a drug encoding network directly on single-cell data using reported optimal hyperparameters.

methods.name: chemCPA-pre
methods.protocol_description: Pretrained version of chemCPA where the drug encoding network was trained on bulk RNA high-throughput screen (L1000). Hyperparameter tuning for adversary parameters was performed.

methods.name: PerturbNet
methods.protocol_description: Model consisting of a perturbation representation network (pretrained on ZINC dataset), a cellular representation network trained on the sci-Plex 3 data, and a mapping network trained on the latent representations from both.

methods.name: GEARS
methods.protocol_description: Baseline for genetic perturbation prediction. Evaluation run using the setting from the GEARS reproducibility repository.

methods.name: naive baseline
methods.protocol_description: For drug response, r2 score evaluated between control unperturbed cells and drug-treated cells.
